resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy & Smoke Certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Berkeley Township Code Enforcement Office (housing inspection), with the Bureau of Fire Prevention (smoke/CO)
requirements: Safe, approved water supply; hot and cold water to sinks and tubs; plumbing fixtures working
Heating equipment properly installed and working
Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet of sleeping areas
Safe, unobstructed exits; entry door deadbolts must not need a key to get out
Floors, foundation, walls, ceilings, doors and windows clean, working and free of dampness; no rodents
Handrail on any stairs with 3 or more steps; safe railings on decks, porches and balconies
Window screens from May 1 to October 1
Kitchen and bathroom floors impervious to water; paint and wallpaper in good condition
Solid core door or sheathing between garage and house; no extension cords or adapters for garage door openers
Roof, walls, windows, gutters, fences, driveway, steps, sidewalks, sheds, garages and bulkheads in good repair
Yard free of litter and debris; lawns and hedges trimmed; trash in approved containers
Street numbers visible from the road; pool fencing to code from original installation
A termite report may be required
All open permits must be closed before the Certificate of Occupancy is issued
Owner or a representative must be on site to operate all utilities

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township of Berkeley Certificate of Occupancy & Smoke Certificate Resale application (with the attached smoke and carbon monoxide certification form) and pay before the housing inspection; checks payable to Berkeley Township. Applications can also be picked up at the Code Enforcement Office, 627 Pinewald-Keswick Rd, Bayville, Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4 pm. Someone must be at the property at the inspection time. A failed inspection needs a $50 reinspection fee before it is rescheduled.

evidence.quote: Any time you rent or sell your home in Berkeley Township, you must apply for a Certificate of Occupancy. For rental property owners, this applies every time the tenant changes.
All transfers of Titles, Rentals, and Resales in age-restricted communities require an original approval letter from the Homeowners Association. (Original signature - no duplicates or copies).

A Certificate of Occupancy (CO) is required when anyone is selling or renting a home. Applications can be picked up at the Code Enforcement Office, Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4 pm. Please feel free to contact our office with any questions, complaints, concerns, or comments at 732-244-7400, ext. 1506.
Kenneth Anderson Supervising Code Enforcement Officer

resale_co.notes: Berkeley combines the resale Certificate of Occupancy and the smoke/CO certificate into one $150 application (fees effective April 8, 2024: resale or rental CO and smoke certificate $150, Transfer of Title $100, reinspection $50). The Transfer of Title application is for non-habitable dwellings only. Resale applications ask for an Ocean County Health Department well certificate if a well is the primary water source, a tight-tank certificate if there is an oil tank, and a flood elevation certificate if in a flood zone. Age-restricted communities need an original HOA approval letter. The applicant must initial that it is their responsibility to research added assessments, open permits and vacant property registration fees. Rentals need a CO at every tenant change. Clerical Assistant: Lisa Buchanan, lbuchanan@berkeleytownship.org. The leads file website (twp.berkeley.nj.us) now redirects to berkeleytownship.org. Page 1 of the Resales Application PDF is a scanned image that was read visually (page 2 has a text layer), so an automatic text check will not find the page 1 quotes ($150 resale fee line, flood elevation review fee, payment and reinspection lines); the $150, $50 and $100 fees are also on the Code Enforcement web page.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level including the basement (not attic or crawl space) and outside each separate sleeping area, located per NFPA 72
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units (since January 1, 2019); hardwired alarms from original construction must not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of the bedrooms if the home has a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage (UL 2034; battery, hardwired or plug-in)
Inspected by a Township inspector as part of the combined resale Certificate of Occupancy

fire_cert.notes: Berkeley is its own fire code enforcing agency (registry code M) through the Township Fire Prevention Bureau. There is no separate published smoke certificate fee: the smoke/CO certificate is bundled into the $150 resale Certificate of Occupancy and Smoke Certificate fee. The Township's smoke form and requirement sheet do not mention a fire extinguisher. Fire Prevention Specialists (same ext. 1236): Callan Cotta, Gabriel Martinez, John Pasola. The three fire companies (Bayville, Manitou Park, Pinewald Pioneer) all fall under the same Township Bureau.
